risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- MD&A Risks and Concerns states employee, input and raw material costs have continued to increase unprecedentedly, and the Threats section calls the surge in raw material, services, power and fuel costs a continuing point of concern - a direct margin risk for a spice-extract business with no pricing power disclosed.
- Heavy rains and other climatic changes have made it hard to obtain agricultural inputs on time and threatened their timely availability, exposing the company to crop-cycle and weather-driven supply interruption in chilli and turmeric feedstock.
- Management flags newly introduced regulatory norms in the spices market as a significant challenge; the secretarial audit also lists the Spices Board Act, Food Safety and Standards Act, Essential Commodity Act, Boilers Act and Explosives Act as specifically applicable, so compliance surface is wide relative to the company's size.
- Management states government intervention on spice import and export is causing upheavals in the market, affecting both demand and price - material because the company describes itself as an exporter.
- The MD&A segment note states the company has no other segment or products and is mainly involved in trading of Other Agricultural Products, so there is no diversification to absorb a shock in the spice/oleoresin chain.
- The unorganised segment has dominated the Indian spices market for many years due to a large number of local players selling open and unbranded products, which caps pricing and branding power for organised participants.
- Management explicitly names the war in Ukraine as causing significant challenges for cost and supply chain.
- The Directors' Report states that risk management under section 134(3)(n) and SEBI LODR is 'Not applicable to the Company', so structural risks are managed only through internal financial controls and Board review rather than a constituted risk framework.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Venture into the ready-to-eat food segment, which management identifies as a large opportunity adjacent to its oleoresin range
- Position oleoresins as a food flavouring agent into processed meat, confectionery and baked-food demand
- Use a stock-exchange listing to open access to capital for expansion plans and entry into new businesses
- Retain talent through competitive salaries and benefits, an inclusive work culture, flexibility and growth opportunities, scaling human capital in line with demand
